chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Yaqub ibn Ja'far, who said:
I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Upon each nostril of the animals is a shaytan. So whenever one of you wishes to bridle it, let him name Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.فَلْيُسَمِّ اللَّهَ: Let him name Allah (invoke His name)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended practice when bridling an animal according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) highlights the Shia concept of spiritual permeation in the physical world, attributing a shaytan to each nostril of beasts to explain their instinctive behaviors. It prescribes the recitation of Allah's name (tasmiyah) during bridling as a protective measure, reflecting the practical application of spiritual awareness in daily interactions with animals. This practice underscores the belief that mundane actions, when accompanied by divine invocation, serve to neutralize spiritual influences.
